# completeness {.divider}

If $\nvdash_\Sigma \varphi$, then $\varphi$ fails at a world of the canonical model $\mathcal{M}_\Sigma$. Which frames does this give us countermodels in?

## completeness of $\textsf{K}$

::: {.theorem}
If $\models \varphi$, then $\vdash_{\textsf{K}} \varphi$.
:::

::: {.proof}
::: {.incremental}
- Suppose $\nvdash_{\textsf{K}} \varphi$. Then $\neg \varphi$ is $\textsf{K}$-consistent.

- By Lindenbaum's lemma, $\{\neg\varphi\}$ extends to a maximal $\textsf{K}$-consistent set $\Gamma$.

- $\Gamma \in W_{\textsf{K}}$, and by the truth lemma $\mathcal{M}_{\textsf{K}}, \Gamma \Vdash \neg \varphi$.

- So $\varphi$ fails at a world of a model based on a frame. Hence $\not\models \varphi$.
:::
:::

## beyond $\textsf{K}$

![](images/strategy.svg){.nostretch width="80%" fig-align="center"}

For $\textsf{KT}$, the same argument yields a world of $\mathcal{M}_{\textsf{KT}}$ where $\varphi$ fails. This shows $\not\models_{\text{ref}} \varphi$ **only if** the canonical frame for $\textsf{KT}$ is reflexive.

## completeness of $\textsf{KT}$ {.smaller}

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="62%"}
::: {.theorem}
If $\models_{\text{ref}} \varphi$, then $\vdash_{\textsf{KT}} \varphi$.
:::

::: {.proof}
It suffices to verify that $\Gamma R_{\textsf{KT}} \Gamma$ for every $\Gamma \in W_{\textsf{KT}}$, i.e.:

- if $\varphi \in \Gamma$, then $\Diamond \varphi \in \Gamma$.

Let $\varphi \in \Gamma$. Since $\vdash_{\textsf{KT}} \varphi \to \Diamond \varphi$, we have $\varphi \to \Diamond \varphi \in \Gamma$. By closure, $\Diamond \varphi \in \Gamma$.
:::
:::

::: {.column width="38%"}
![](images/c-ref.svg){width="100%"}
:::
:::

# canonicity {.divider}

## canonical axioms and systems

::: {.definition}
A normal system $\Sigma$ is **canonical** iff the canonical frame for $\Sigma$ validates every theorem of $\Sigma$.
:::

. . .

::: {.definition}
An axiom is **canonical** iff for every normal system $\Sigma$ containing all its substitution instances, the canonical frame for $\Sigma$ validates it.
:::

. . .

Canonical axioms are what make completeness proofs *modular*: they can be combined freely.

## five canonical axioms

::: {.theorem}
If $\Sigma$ contains every substitution instance of the axiom, then $R_\Sigma$ satisfies the corresponding condition.
:::

| | axiom | condition on $R_\Sigma$ |
|--|--|--|
| $\textsf{D}$ | $\Box p \to \Diamond p$ | serial |
| $\textsf{T}$ | $\Box p \to p$ | reflexive |
| $\textsf{B}$ | $p \to \Box \Diamond p$ | symmetric |
| $\textsf{4}$ | $\Box p \to \Box \Box p$ | transitive |
| $\textsf{5}$ | $\Diamond p \to \Box \Diamond p$ | euclidean |

## the pattern

In each case, we must show that $R_\Sigma$ holds between certain maximal consistent sets.

::: {.incremental}
- Unpack the condition using the definition of $R_\Sigma$ (in its $\Box$ or $\Diamond$ form).

- Use the axiom, which belongs to every $\Gamma \in W_\Sigma$, to move a formula from one set to another.

- In the diagrams, solid arrows are given and the dashed arrow is to be shown.
:::

## $\textsf{D}$: seriality {.smaller}

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="60%"}
Need: for every $\Gamma$ there is $\Delta$ with $\{\varphi : \Box\varphi \in \Gamma\} \subseteq \Delta$. It suffices that $\{\varphi : \Box\varphi \in \Gamma\}$ is $\Sigma$-consistent.

::: {.proof}
Suppose not. Then $\vdash_\Sigma (\varphi_1 \wedge \dots \wedge \varphi_n) \to \bot$ for some $\Box\varphi_1, \dots, \Box\varphi_n \in \Gamma$. By normality, $\vdash_\Sigma (\Box\varphi_1 \wedge \dots \wedge \Box\varphi_n) \to \Box \bot$, so $\Box\bot \in \Gamma$. By $\textsf{D}$, $\Diamond \bot \in \Gamma$. But $\vdash_\Sigma \Box \neg \bot$, i.e., $\neg\Diamond\bot \in \Gamma$. So $\Gamma$ is $\Sigma$-inconsistent.
:::
:::

::: {.column width="40%"}
![](images/c-ser.svg){width="100%"}
:::
:::

## $\textsf{B}$: symmetry {.smaller}

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
Need: if $\Gamma R_\Sigma \Delta$, then $\Delta R_\Sigma \Gamma$, i.e.,

- if $\{\varphi : \Box\varphi \in \Gamma\} \subseteq \Delta$, then $\{\Diamond \varphi : \varphi \in \Gamma\} \subseteq \Delta$.

::: {.proof}
Let $\varphi \in \Gamma$. By $\textsf{B}$, $\varphi \to \Box \Diamond \varphi \in \Gamma$, so $\Box\Diamond\varphi \in \Gamma$. Since $\Gamma R_\Sigma \Delta$, $\Diamond \varphi \in \Delta$.
:::
:::

::: {.column width="45%"}
![](images/c-sym.svg){width="100%"}
:::
:::

## $\textsf{4}$: transitivity {.smaller}

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
Need: if $\Gamma R_\Sigma \Delta$ and $\Delta R_\Sigma \Theta$, then $\Gamma R_\Sigma \Theta$, i.e.,

- if $\Box \varphi \in \Gamma$, then $\varphi \in \Theta$.

::: {.proof}
Let $\Box \varphi \in \Gamma$. By $\textsf{4}$, $\Box\Box\varphi \in \Gamma$. Since $\Gamma R_\Sigma \Delta$, $\Box \varphi \in \Delta$. Since $\Delta R_\Sigma \Theta$, $\varphi \in \Theta$.
:::
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/c-trans.svg){width="100%"}
:::
:::

## $\textsf{5}$: euclideanness {.smaller}

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
Need: if $\Gamma R_\Sigma \Delta$ and $\Gamma R_\Sigma \Theta$, then $\Delta R_\Sigma \Theta$, i.e.,

- if $\varphi \in \Theta$, then $\Diamond\varphi \in \Delta$.

::: {.proof}
Let $\varphi \in \Theta$. Since $\Gamma R_\Sigma \Theta$, $\Diamond\varphi \in \Gamma$. By $\textsf{5}$, $\Box\Diamond\varphi \in \Gamma$. Since $\Gamma R_\Sigma \Delta$, $\Diamond \varphi \in \Delta$.
:::
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/c-eucl.svg){width="100%"}
:::
:::

# completeness for the landscape {.divider}

## combining canonical axioms

::: {.theorem}
If $\Sigma$ is axiomatized by canonical axioms corresponding to conditions $C_1, \dots, C_n$, then $\Sigma$ is complete with respect to the class of frames satisfying $C_1, \dots, C_n$.
:::

. . .

::: {.proof}
If $\nvdash_\Sigma \varphi$, then $\varphi$ fails in $\mathcal{M}_\Sigma$. Since each axiom is canonical, the canonical frame satisfies each of $C_1, \dots, C_n$.
:::

. . .

For example, $R_{\textsf{S4}}$ is reflexive and transitive, and $R_{\textsf{S5}}$ is reflexive and euclidean.

## the full picture

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/landscape.svg){width="100%"}
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/landscape-rel.svg){width="100%"}
:::
:::

Combined with soundness, each system in the landscape **characterizes** the corresponding class of frames.
